purpose: Round-5 study slots (track 1), main job at 48 trajectories per half (fits a 40 GB card): slot encoders with memory on raw gliders level 0, 2000 steps, up to 14 configs in priority order (supervised capacity control, closure, warm start, reconstruction, local law, no k-means prior, classic slot AE)
notes: Replaces r5-slots-006 (cancelled before start, $0): identical request (same ref 7099a0ded, same env including XLA_PYTHON_CLIENT_MEM_FRACTION=0.9, same types and limits); only cap_usd is raised from 18.75 to 21.80, because the one offer that was rentable (H100_80GB via datacrunch at $5.0199/h, on which r5-foundry-001 ran at 05:10 UTC) missed the old cap by 7 cents: 5.0199 x 3.75 = $18.82. The new cap admits offers up to $5.78/h at max_hours 3.5. Expected spend: about $7.50 on an A100_40GB at $1.99/h (the full 3.5 h), about $12 on that H100 (all 14 configs in about 2.3 h, then the job ends early). r5-slots-005 itself replaced r5-slots-004 (cancelled before any pod existed: no A100_80GB / H100_80GB / H200_141GB could be rented for more than two hours). SAME code, pinned by the same ref 7099a0ded (reviewed clean by the Mac for r5-slots-004; CPU test of job.sh end to end at tiny size from a git archive of these six paths at that commit: 14 configs, 124 halves certified, exit 0, FAIL=0). Only the env, the GPU types and the limits differ. S5_SIZE=pilot: 48 trajectories per half (16 certification + 32 training-only, 4 for validation), the size of r5-slots-003; the doubled data of the full size is dropped so that the job fits a 40 GB card. Memory: resident device data about 5.2 GiB (measured in r5-slots-003) plus training temporaries of up to about 24.7 GiB for the rec configs and far less for sup / set / self (the Mac's estimate for this code), so about 30 GiB at the peak; preallocation stays off. An out-of-memory or any other error in one config is caught in strain.main (the config goes to train_errors.txt, compiled functions are released, the next config runs; latents, training records and certification of the other configs are written; the job then exits non-zero). Device arrays are far below 2^31 elements at this size (largest 4.7e8). Timing is set for the SLOWER card. Measured on the H200 at this size (r5-slots-003): reference stage 570 s including a no-learning encoder that is now dropped, 9.6 s per 100 training steps, 90-165 s compile per config. Assuming the A100 is 2.6 times slower on the GPU part: reference stage about 1300 s, a config about 1000 s (2000 steps about 500 s, compile about 250 s, encoding and objective values about 250 s). Time limits in seconds from the start of job.sh: training stops at 10400, no new certification item after 11200, workers killed at 11900; max_hours 3.5 = 12600 s. No config starts with under 1000 s left before the training deadline (S5_CFG_MIN_S), so a started config is expected to train all its steps; S5_CFG_MAX_S=1500 only stops a config that runs far over. Expected to finish: on an A100 (40 or 80 GB) the first 9 configs (sam_sup, sam_set, sam_set_ws, sam_rec, sam_self, sgm_set, sgc_rec, sac_set, sam_set_dg), at least the first 7 if the card is slower than assumed; the first 5 are the ones the study's question needs; on an H100 all 14 in about 2.3 h, after which the job ends early. Skipped configs are recorded in train_done.json. Budget: study cap $25, $3.13 billed so far (r5-slots-004, 005 and 006 were cancelled before any pod existed, $0 each); this cap $21.80 keeps the total under $25 in the worst case. No network or subprocess use outside setup; job.sh starts its own CPU certification workers.
